newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sees no change in Cuba policy after China vote.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sees no change in Cuba policy after China vote.

text.p: Fresh from winning a key congressional vote to retain open trade relations with communist China, the White House on Tuesday said it would oppose any measure to lift an embargo on Cuba.

U.S. National Security Adviser Sandy Berger said there were historical and practical differences between China and Cuba to justify President Bill Clinton's policy of engagement with China but not for Cuba.

"At this point in our view to eliminate that embargo would not have a liberalising effect on the Cuban regime," Berger told a news briefing. "Quite the contrary, it would solidify a regime that has had an opportunity to reform over the last 35 years and has not."
Berger was responding to a reporter's question following a U.S. House of Representatives vote to maintain Most Favoured Nation (MFN) status with China, leaving lower tariffs in place.
Administration opponents advocated removing the trade benefits as a way to pressure China on improving human rights and to stop weapons proliferation.
Berger did not refer to a bipartisan proposal last week to lift an embargo on food and medicine to Cuba in a bid to help children, the sick and the elderly.

When eight Democrats and four Republicans in the House proposed the food and medicine exemption last week, the White House said it would examine the proposed legislation carefully given that the Cuban embargo makes provisions for humanitarian aid.
